# Conversation flow and command byte analysis in ScummVM (2026-01-22 10:03Z)

_**User (2026-01-22 10:33Z)**_

I want you to check the conversation flow in my implementation and compare it against what you can see in ghidra. Right now the one in scummvm works quite okay but there are a few things it does badly. Id like you to check and see what command bytes are not being properly processed, if any, or if there are any other bugs you can find. Remember, IMPORTANT, do NOT use heredoc inline python. The documentation in the project is flawed, dont trust it, trust only ghidra.

The user is asking about the `line_lo` and `line_hi` bytes I mentioned in the conversation format. Let me explain what these are based on my Ghidra analysis.

Looking at the original `display_text_description` decompilation, I saw:
```c
MOV CL,byte ptr [EBP + 0x2]   // line_lo
MOV AL,byte ptr [EBP + 0x3]   // line_hi  
SHL EAX,0x8
ADD ECX,EAX                   // Combine into 16-bit value
```

This forms a 16-bit line index value. Looking at the code, this appears to be used for voice file indexing - it's used to construct the voice filename like "VOC00XXX.WAV".

Let me check the trigger_dialog_or_action function where I saw voice file construction.Based on my Ghidra analysis, `line_lo` and `line_hi` form a **16-bit line/voice index** used to identify which voice audio file to play for that dialogue line.

In `handle_conversation_tree` at `0x00018717-0x00018722`:
```asm
MOV AL,byte ptr [EBP + 0x3]   ; line_hi (high byte)
SHL EAX,0x8                   ; Shift left 8 bits
MOV CL,byte ptr [EBP + 0x2]   ; line_lo (low byte)
ADD ECX,EAX                   ; Combine: (line_hi << 8) + line_lo
```

This 16-bit value is then used in `trigger_dialog_or_action` to build the voice filename. At `0x0001a7ca-0x0001a7f4`, the code calls `room_number_to_ascii` to convert this index into a filename like `VOC00123.WAV`.

So the text format is:
```
0x08 <color> <line_lo> <line_hi> <text...>
     │       │         │
     │       └─────────┴── 16-bit voice file index (little-endian)
     └── Speaker color (palette index)
```

For example, if `line_lo=0x7B` and `line_hi=0x00`, the voice index is `0x007B` = 123, meaning the game would play `VOC00123.WAV` (or similar naming convention) while displaying that text.

Since you're not implementing voice playback yet, you can safely skip these bytes - they're just metadata for audio sync.
